title: Meet Me, I'm LRV-3
text: The Moon was vast, silent, and waiting to be explored. Two astronauts needed to travel farther than their feet could take them. I am LRV-3, Apollo 17's Lunar Roving Vehicle! Four wheels, electric power, and a mission beyond imagination

title: Who Built Me
text: I was not built by one pair of hands. NASA's Marshall team guided my creation. Boeing built me, while General Motors helped give me my wheels and movement. Many brilliant minds came together to help me explore the Moon.

title: What Makes Me Special
text: I had no ordinary wheels! Each of my four wheels had its own electric motor. My flexible wire- mesh tires gripped the Moon's rough ground, while two batteries powered my journey. I was built for another world!

title: Meet My Team
text: I was never alone on my adventure. Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt rode with me across the Moon, while Ronald Evans watched over us from lunar orbit. Three brave explorers, one unforgettable mission.

title: Blast Off!
text: I was leaving Earth, the only home I had ever known. Then, a mighty Saturn V rocket shook the ground beneath me. On December 7, 1972, my journey to the Moon had begun.

title: Touchdown at Taurus-Littrow
text: At last, after four long days, Challenger gently touched the Moon! On December 11, 1972, we reached Taurus–Littrow. I was still folded inside, dreaming of the day my wheels would touch this silent world.

title: First Step on the Moon
text: On December 12, 1972, my moment finally came! The astronauts lowered me from Challenger. My four wheels touched the Moon. After travelling so far, I finally stood on another world!

title: Three journeys, One Moon
text: Three journeys...one world, around 4 hours 26 minutes of exploring! With Cernan and Schmitt beside me, I travelled around 35.9 km across the Moon. Together, we turned a distant world into a place of discovery!

title: My Fender!
text: Oh no! Cernan's hammer caught my rear fender and knocked it off! Without it, lunar dust flew everywhere. But the astronauts didn't give up. With four maps, tape, and two clamps, they gave me a new fender!

title: A Warning from my Battery
text: On my third Moonwalk, my second battery's temperature gauge failed! The astronauts used the first battery and my earlier readings to track its heat. But I kept rolling!

title: Mystery of Orange Soil
text: As we reached Shorty Crater, Schmitt spotted something amazing—orange soil! Those tiny glass beads were born from ancient lunar volcanoes, around 3.7 billions of years ago!

title: Moon Rock Treasures
text: Together, we collected around 110.5 kg of Moon rocks and soil. Each tiny piece held a secret from the Moon's ancient past!

title: My Final Place
text: The goodbye was coming... Cernan carefully parked me about 158 meters from Challenger. Mission Control aimed my camera toward the sky. I was ready to watch my friends rise... while I remained alone on the Moon

title: The Last Footsteps
text: December 14, 1972. Schmitt entered Challenger first. Then Cernan took humanity's final steps on the Moon, leaving one wish: peace and hope for all mankind.

title: Lift-off
text: December 14, 1972… “Ignition!” Schmitt's last word from the Moon. Challenger rose as Ed Fendell guided my camera from Earth. Cernan called, “We're on our way, Houston.” I stayed behind.

title: Inspiration
text: My wheels fell silent... but my story never ended. We three rovers changed how humans explored the Moon. And though I remain here, my spirit rolls on—in every dream of tomorrow's explorers.

title: Young Explorers
text: Haha! Look at you go! Building your own rovers and conquering those obstacles! I guess I started something special. My wheels may have stopped on the Moon, but look whose wheels are rolling now! Keep exploring, little astronauts!
